clue.text: Father about heartless performance: 'It's supposed to be funny'

indicators.note: the father's word goes around the other piece, sitting about it

parts.note: a sire is a father, especially of an animal

indicators.note: the word for performance loses its central letter, its heart

parts.note: an act is a performance on stage

explanation.surface: A dad slags off a soulless show while insisting it is meant to be a comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon and quotation marks make the definition look like a line spoken by the father.
explanation.definitionFit: Satire is a genre of writing or performance whose purpose is to mock through humour.

clue.text: Mess made by quiet group in school

indicators.note: the quiet and group letters go inside the school abbreviation

parts.note: P is piano, the musical term for quiet
a lot is a group or set of things

explanation.surface: A quiet bunch of pupils leaves a mess at school.
explanation.definitionFit: A splotch is a messy blot or smear, so it names a spilled or spattered mark.

clue.text: Take a walk, parking vehicle first

indicators.note: the vehicle goes first, ahead of the parking letter

parts.note: a tram is a vehicle running on rails
P is the usual sign and abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Someone opts to stroll, leaving the car parked first.
explanation.definitionFit: To tramp is to walk heavily or hike a long way, so it means going for a walk.

clue.text: A learner missing from practice picks up again?

indicators.note: the A and the learner are taken out of the practice word

parts.note: a rehearsal is a practice run of a performance
L is the learner plate on a British car

explanation.surface: With one novice absent, a rehearsal restarts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picks up' is used in the sense of hearing something, so the definition means hears once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick up a sound is to hear it, and rehears means hears a second time, as a court rehears a case.

clue.text: More than one mountain creature in the same place gets very cold

parts.note: ib. is the short form of ibidem, Latin for 'in the same place', used in footnotes
ices means freezes, becomes very cold

explanation.surface: Goats sharing one Alpine spot are freezing.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibex is a wild mountain goat; its plural is ibices, so this means several of those animals.

clue.text: Insect and nothing more, Spooner's said, in drinking vessel

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner's habit was swapping the opening sounds of a pair of words

parts.note: mere means nothing more than
a bug is an insect

explanation.surface: A bug and nothing else, as the Reverend Spooner put it, in a cup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mere bug' with its opening sounds swapped is said as 'beer mug'.
explanation.definitionFit: A beer mug is a large handled cup for drinking ale, a kind of drinking vessel.

clue.text: New income set to provide a small amount of money

indicators.note: the letters are made new, reworked into a different order

explanation.surface: A fresh earnings target produces only a little cash.
explanation.definitionFit: The centesimo was a hundredth of an Italian lira, a coin of tiny value.

clue.text: Half the people looking to catch us have a sneaking feeling

indicators.note: the half-word captures the other piece, holding it inside
only the first half of the people looking is used

parts.note: spectators are people watching an event

explanation.surface: Fifty percent of onlookers want to nab us, a nagging hunch says.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half' takes the first five of the ten letters of the onlookers' word, and 'to catch' wraps that around the given pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspect something is to believe it without proof, a hunch or sneaking feeling.

clue.text: Militant Millicent, reportedly one turned on by Americans

indicators.note: what is heard said is her surname, which is how the answer is pronounced

parts.note: Millicent Fawcett was a leading campaigner for British women's votes

explanation.surface: A campaigning woman is, so they say, someone Americans get excited by.
explanation.walkthrough: Millicent Fawcett led the British suffrage movement. 'turned on' suggests excitement but means a tap being opened.
explanation.definitionFit: Faucet is the American word for a tap, which one turns on to get water.

clue.text: He's declared sane after treatment, in a state of being mentally alert

definitions.text: a state of being mentally alert

indicators.note: the letters are worked on and come out rearranged, as a patient is changed by treatment

explanation.surface: A patient is certified sane after therapy and is now sharp-witted.
explanation.definitionFit: Being clear-headed means thinking lucidly, so the noun names a condition of alert, sensible thought.

clue.text: More work here, more pleasure here?

definitions.text: More work here, more pleasure here?

parts.words: More work here, more pleasure here?
parts.note: Thomas More's best-known work is the book named after an imagined ideal place, where one would expect more pleasure

explanation.surface: A puzzled remark about a place that offers both extra toil and extra delight.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitalised More is Sir Thomas More, whose 1516 book named this ideal island; the second 'more' is the ordinary word, so the place is a paradise.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of More's book became the general word for an imagined perfect society.

clue.text: Like some roads with bit of confusion — two traffic lights but only one right!

indicators.note: only a small piece, the opening letter, of confusion is used
the two colours share an R between them, so one of the pair is dropped

parts.note: amber and red are two of the lights on a traffic signal

explanation.surface: A muddled motorist complains about a junction showing two signal colours yet only one right turn.
explanation.walkthrough: The two colours run together share a doubled R at their join; 'but only one' keeps just one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: A cambered road is curved, higher at the centre than at the sides, so water drains off.

clue.text: Dense group of trees in which little son hides

indicators.note: the group of trees is the place into which the other piece goes
the son conceals himself within the trees, so his letter sits inside

parts.note: a thicket is a dense clump of trees or shrubs
S is the short form of son

explanation.surface: A small boy hides in a tight cluster of trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Thickset means heavily or closely built, so it can stand for compact or dense.

clue.text: Officer studies information, schematically presented

parts.note: to con is to study or pore over, so cons means studies
a table sets out data in rows and columns

explanation.surface: A policeman pores over data shown as a chart.
explanation.definitionFit: A constable is a police officer of the lowest rank in Britain.

clue.text: Fellow, one left being given time inside, shown to be this?

indicators.note: these letters are placed within the word for fellow

parts.note: guy is a casual word for a man or fellow
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A man left alone is sent to prison, and the sentence proves what he is.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is close to all-in-one: a fellow given 'time' (a prison sentence) has been found guilty.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone given a jail term has been proven culpable by a court, so the answer is the verdict.

clue.text: Portraying an image of a type of chemical bond involving carbon

indicators.note: the word for the bond takes in the carbon letter, enclosing it

parts.note: an ionic bond is a chemical bond formed by attraction between charged ions
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: A chemistry note describes a picture of a bond containing carbon.
explanation.definitionFit: Something iconic relates to or acts as an icon, a picture or representation.

clue.text: Queen being grabbed by womaniser in court game

indicators.note: the whole goes inside the abbreviation for court
the queen is seized by the womaniser, so her letter sits inside his word

parts.note: a roué is a debauched man, a rake
Q is the short form of queen, as in chess

explanation.surface: A monarch is seized by a rake at court during a lawn game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court game' looks like the definition, but 'court' gives CT around the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Croquet is a lawn game played by hitting balls through hoops with mallets.

clue.text: Draw together as in an intimate photograph

definitions.meaning: to come closer together, narrowing a gap
a picture taken from very near the subject

explanation.surface: Huddle up, as people do for a snap taken at short range.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses rest on nearness: moving into a tight space and a shot at short distance.

clue.text: Trees we'd chopped in small areas of land

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go inside the units of land

parts.note: a rood is an old unit of land area, a quarter of an acre

indicators.note: the short word is cut up and its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone says we would fell trees in little plots.
explanation.walkthrough: The rood is an old English measure of land, a quarter of an acre; the rearranged letters of the short word sit just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Redwoods are huge Californian conifers, the sequoias, so they are an example of trees.

clue.text: On a bike, one's headed North, East or West?

definitions.text: one's headed North, East or West?
definitions.meaning: Yorkshire was divided into three ..., named North, East and West

explanation.surface: A cyclist wonders which way to head.
explanation.walkthrough: The old county of Yorkshire in England had three districts, the North, East and West Ridings; each is one 'headed' by such a direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding means mounted on a bike or horse, and is also the name for a Yorkshire district.

clue.text: Some Eden with love gone, abandoned territory

indicators.note: the love letter is to be taken away from the words
the remaining letters are left unruly and rearranged

parts.note: love means zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A part of paradise, now loveless and deserted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone' removes O from SOME EDEN; 'abandoned' rearranges the rest, SMEEDEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A demesne is an estate or domain held by a lord, so it is land one owns or controls.

clue.text: Misery of endless want keeping the old man in

indicators.note: the shortened word holds the father inside
the word for want loses its final letter

parts.note: to desire is to want
pa is a familiar word for father, the old man

explanation.surface: The unhappiness of constant craving traps Dad at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The old man' is familiar slang for one's father, here the short word for dad.
explanation.definitionFit: Despair is utter hopelessness, a deep wretchedness close to misery.

clue.text: Roman emperor, hiding in enclosure, secured position

indicators.note: the emperor conceals himself within the enclosure, so his name sits inside

parts.note: a fold is a pen for sheep
Otho was a Roman emperor for a few months in AD 69

explanation.surface: An emperor lurking in a sheep pen has found himself a safe spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A foothold is a secure place to stand, and figuratively a firm position gained to build on.

clue.text: Spy on street creating trouble

indicators.note: the spy is placed on, ahead of, the street in an across answer

parts.note: a mole is a spy planted inside an organisation

explanation.surface: An undercover agent out on the road is stirring up difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: To molest is to pester or harass, so in older usage it means to bother or disturb someone.

clue.text: Irish water in sunless bog

indicators.note: S, the abbreviation for sun, is removed from the word

parts.note: a slough is a swamp or bog

explanation.surface: An Irish lake lies in a dark marsh.
explanation.definitionFit: A lough is the Irish word for a lake or sea inlet, like the Scottish loch.

clue.text: Ban duke? Squabble about some rehashed stuff

indicators.note: the letters are turned about, put into a new order

explanation.surface: A row about banning an aristocrat, recycled again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: BUBBLE AND SQUEAK is a British dish of leftover potato and cabbage fried together.
explanation.definitionFit: The dish is made from reheated leftovers, so it is literally food cooked up again.

clue.text: Idiots in European port missing an entrance to shipping

indicators.note: the port's name lacks the given little word

parts.note: Antwerp is a major port in Belgium

indicators.note: only the opening letter of shipping is used

explanation.surface: Fools in a Belgian harbour city fail to find the way in for the ships.
explanation.definitionFit: Twerps are silly or annoying people, a mild British insult for fools.

clue.text: Ogle, needing to grab companion? Well he might!

indicators.note: the word for ogle seizes the other piece, holding it inside

parts.note: to leer is to look at someone lustfully, to ogle
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: Someone eyes up and wants to seize a partner, and of course a lecher would.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition comments on the rest: a man who ogles and grabs is just what the answer is.
explanation.definitionFit: A lecher is a lustful man, exactly the sort who would leer and grope.
